summary_html: A **parent/guardian/child requests help** without a substantiated allegation. FFPSA created a federal pathway for **prevention services** to avert removal and stabilize families before a case escalates.
authority_html: - **Family First Prevention Services Act (2018)** — prevention services, kinship support; shifts upstream from removal to support

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court held that a parent may voluntarily transfer permanent legal and physical custody to a relative for good cause, but that on this record the earlier transfer was involuntary and therefore triggered the presumption of palpable unfitness.
key_cases.relevance: It recognizes the parent-initiated route by which a family can place a child with a relative without a contested adjudication.
key_cases.quote: because such a transfer of custody is a statutorily approved permanency disposition, we conclude that a parent may voluntarily transfer custody to a relative for good cause

key_cases.case_name: In re Welfare of Child of M.K.
key_cases.holding: The court held that parents were entitled to withdraw CHIPS admissions that the county obtained by threatening to withhold needed services, because accepting admissions extracted that way was a manifest injustice.
key_cases.relevance: Parents who approached the county seeking help for their child were pressed into admitting statutory grounds; the court held that coercion unenforceable.
key_cases.quote: we conclude that a threat to act in a manner that is not in a child's best interests constitutes a manifest injustice

state_agency.name: Minnesota Department of Children, Youth, and Families
state_agency.hotline: No statewide hotline. Call the county or Tribal child protection agency where the child lives — the directory link is on dcyf.mn.gov/individuals-and-families/report-abuse

A professional or professional's delegate engaged in the practice of the healing arts — Minn. Stat. § 260E.06, subd. 1(a)(1)

A professional or professional's delegate engaged in social services, including employee assistance counseling and guardian ad litem and parenting time expeditor services — Minn. Stat. § 260E.06, subd. 1(a)(1) and (b)
A professional or professional's delegate engaged in hospital administration — Minn. Stat. § 260E.06, subd. 1(a)(1)
A professional or professional's delegate engaged in psychological or psychiatric treatment — Minn. Stat. § 260E.06, subd. 1(a)(1)
A professional or professional's delegate engaged in child care — Minn. Stat. § 260E.06, subd. 1(a)(1)
A professional or professional's delegate engaged in education — Minn. Stat. § 260E.06, subd. 1(a)(1)
A professional or professional's delegate engaged in correctional supervision or probation and correctional services — Minn. Stat. § 260E.06, subd. 1(a)(1)
A professional or professional's delegate engaged in law enforcement — Minn. Stat. § 260E.06, subd. 1(a)(1)
A member of the clergy who received the information while engaged in ministerial duties, except information privileged under § 595.02, subd. 1(c) — Minn. Stat. § 260E.06, subd. 1(a)(2)

An employee or supervisor of a private or public youth recreation program (including coaching staff), as to abuse by another employee or supervisor or abuse a child discloses — Minn. Stat. § 260E.055, subd. 1(d) and subd. 2

A parent, guardian, or caretaker relying on spiritual means or prayer in lieu of medical care, when the lack of medical care may cause serious danger to the child's health — Minn. Stat. § 260E.06, subd. 3

timeline_requirements.deadline: Except in a noncaregiver human trafficking assessment: immediately if sexual abuse or substantial child endangerment is alleged; within 5 calendar days for all other screened in reports
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified by statute; Minn. Stat. § 260E.20, subd. 2(b) sets the face-to-face contact deadline for the local welfare agency.
timeline_requirements.extension_grounds: Face-to-face contact on a report alleging sexual abuse or substantial child endangerment may be postponed for no more than five calendar days if the child is residing in a location confirmed to restrict contact with the alleged offender, or if the local welfare agency is pursuing a court order for the caregiver to produce the child for questioning under Minn. Stat. § 260E.22, subd. 5 (§ 260E.20, subd. 2(b)).

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified by statute; Minn. Stat. § 260E.24, subd. 1 requires the local welfare agency to conclude the assessment or investigation within 45 days.
timeline_requirements.extension_grounds: Only to complete a criminal investigation or to receive expert information requested within 45 days of receipt of the report (Minn. Stat. § 260E.24, subd. 1).
